result:
There is a quiet magic in the first twenty minutes of a morning before the rest of the world wakes up. It is a fragile kind of silence, untouched by the hum of traffic, the ping of notifications, or the collective anxiety of a busy day. In this narrow window, the air feels different—crisp, still, and full of potential. 

I like to sit by the window with a mug of coffee that is far too hot, watching the light slowly bleed into the sky. It usually starts as a bruised purple, softens into a bruised pink, and finally settles into a pale, honest gold. Trees stand like ink blots against the horizon, gradually revealing the intricate lace of their branches. 

We spend so much of our lives rushing. We chase deadlines, accumulate tasks, and measure our worth by our output. But dawn doesn't rush. It doesn't apologize for taking its time. It reminds us that transitions are natural and that darkness always yields to light, no matter how stubborn the night feels. 

There is comfort in this cyclic rhythm. Long after our small worries and grand ambitions have faded, the sun will still rise, painting the sky with the same indifferent beauty. It makes me feel small, but in the best possible way—a tiny, grateful observer in a vast, breathing universe. And as the first car finally rumbles down the street, breaking the spell, I take one last sip and feel ready to meet the day.
